newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Two groups shortlisted for Olympics indoor stadium.
newsitem.headline: Two groups shortlisted for Olympics indoor stadium.

text.p: The New South Wales state government said on Thursday it had shortlisted two groups for the construction of an indoor sports arena for the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games site in the suburb of Homebush.

State minister for the Olympics, Michael Knight, said one group was known as the Millenium consortium and consisted of Abigroup Ltd, Obayashi, Macquarie Bank Ltd, AIDC Ltd and Cox Richardson Architects.
The other group was the SA2000 Events consortium, comprising Hambros Plc, Bovis McLaughlin, Multiplex Constructions, Ogden IFC and Scott Carver Architects.

"The selection of two proponents followed evaluation by the Olympic Co-ordination Authority (OCA) of detailed proposals for the design, construction, financing, operation and maintenance of the arena from three consortia," Knight said.
The centre would provide a 15,000 seat venue for artistic gymnastics and the finals of the volleyball and handball at the Olympics and would be used for basketball at the Paralympics.
Following the Games, the arena would be used as an entertainment centre providing up to 20,000 seats.
Knight said the OCA had established a program to finish the arena by the end of 1999 to enable an Olympic event to be held beforehand.
He said an agreement with the successful group was expected to be signed by mid-1997 with construction scheduled to start in September 1997.
